support.role: Manually derived validator cases; no executed outputs
support.text:
Conditional on passing the mappings constructed from ENTRIES.json by the supplied expectations helper:

report-valid.md: status valid; declaration.completion "complete"; declaration.report_kind "answer"; all six identity comparisons match; diagnostics empty.
report-mismatch.md: status mismatch; the same completion and kind remain in declaration; target_commit compares the session's forty "a" characters with the report's forty "f" characters, source "pinned session", matches false; one identity_mismatch diagnostic names target_commit. The other five comparisons match.
report-missing.md: status missing; declaration null; comparisons empty; diagnostic reason missing. Its prose saying work is complete does not become a declaration claim.
report-invalid.md: status invalid; declaration null; comparisons empty; diagnostic reason duplicate_key for completion. Neither the first "partial" nor the second "complete" value is selected as the claim.
report-partial-null.md: status valid; declaration.completion "partial"; declaration.report_kind null; six matching comparisons; diagnostics empty. Null is permitted for this partial declaration.
report-prose-variant.md: the same validator result as report-valid.md, because the declaration bytes and comparisons are unchanged and the changed prose introduces no fence effects.

These are source-derived cases, not captured program results. The reports' different byte digests remain stipulated entry metadata; this validator does not receive or check an expected digest. That check, any unavailable-byte branch, and record=None or expected_digest=None behavior at the status entry point remain unaccounted for because the consumer is missing.

support.role: Controls, required distinctions and intentional projection
support.text:
The primary distinguishing pair is report-valid.md versus report-mismatch.md. Only target_commit changes from the pinned value to a different well-formed value. The validator changes valid to mismatch and preserves the conflicting operands and their source; well-formedness does not erase identity mismatch. This supplies a firing comparison for the identity distinction, at the validator only.

report-missing.md versus report-invalid.md supplies a second important pair: both yield declaration null and empty comparisons, but status and diagnostic reason distinguish absent declaration from rejected duplicate keys. Looking only at declaration would erase a required distinction; the complete validator dictionary does not.

report-valid.md versus report-prose-variant.md supplies the invariance case: ordinary commentary outside the identical declaration does not change the structured claims. This is appropriate projection for the stated use, not evidence that arbitrary surrounding bytes can never affect fence parsing.

A further manually reasoned variant of report-partial-null.md deleting the report_kind member would fail at lines 110–111 with missing_field. The supplied explicit null instead remains a valid declaration value. No new variant file was executed. The schema therefore distinguishes explicit null from an absent required member at the validator boundary.

The validator discards parsed declaration contents on invalid input and does not return raw report prose. Those are visible projections, but the named use requires the invalid category and claim provenance, not selection among competing invalid claims or preservation of every report byte. They do not by themselves establish a failure of that use.

The validator returns the report's completion/report_kind inside declaration, separate from validation status. Its code has no process-exit or manager-judgment input and does not infer either from those fields. A valid result means acceptance of the declaration syntax/shape and equality against the expectations actually supplied; it does not establish true completion, a successful process, report quality or manager endorsement. Source strings in comparisons are furnished by the caller and do not themselves prove observation or authenticity. The question stipulates byte reads and identities, while capture and access enforcement are outside scope.

For the missing consumer, inspect exactly how it constructs expected and sources, calls validation, and builds every returned dictionary branch. Follow its actual reads of status, declaration, comparisons and diagnostics, including any nested companion result, before deciding whether a claim omitted at top level is lost. Check that missing versus invalid and mismatch versus valid remain inspectable and that completion/kind remain attributed rather than promoted to execution facts or a manager judgment. Account separately for record=None, expected_digest=None and unavailable/digest-mismatch reads listed in ENTRIES.json.

This would distinguish preservation by retained companion data from lossy projection or unsupported promotion. Until then the manager cannot rely on this investigation as confirmation that the named status view supports the use. No consumer repair or substantive failure is established, and no expansion to collection selection, rendering, producer execution or disposal is needed.
